source: UNESCO, Intangible Cultural Heritage, Representative List: Ramlila, the traditional performance of the Ramayana (inscribed 2008 at 3.COM, Istanbul, 4 to 8 November 2008; originally proclaimed 2005); Durga Puja in Kolkata (inscribed 2021 at 16.COM, held online, 13 to 18 December 2021); Garba of Gujarat (inscribed 2023 at 18.COM, Kasane, Botswana, 5 to 8 December 2023). Deepavali (inscribed 2025 at 20.COM, New Delhi, 8 to 12 December 2025). Element and session pages on ich.unesco.org, read 16 Oct 2026.

beats.vo: Ramlila, Durga Puja, Garba and Deepavali are all on UNESCO's intangible heritage list.
beats.note: Lit: the two states UNESCO names. Ramlila: northern India. Deepavali: across India.

beats.text: UNESCO: “performed across northern India during the festival of Dussehra”; “originally proclaimed in 2005”.
beats.sub: “ten to twelve days” for most Ramlilas
beats.vo: In two thousand eight, UNESCO listed Ramlila, performed across northern India at Dussehra.

beats.text: UNESCO: “an annual festival celebrated in September or October, most notably in Kolkata, in West Bengal”.
beats.sub: days of worship: UNESCO says “the ten-day worship”
beats.vo: In twenty twenty-one came Durga Puja in Kolkata, in West Bengal.

beats.text: UNESCO: “performed on the occasion of the Hindu festival of Navaratri”.
beats.vo: Then, in twenty twenty-three, Garba of Gujarat, a dance performed at Navaratri.

beats.text: UNESCO: “it falls on the new moon in October or November and lasts several days”.
beats.vo: In twenty twenty-five, Deepavali joined, at UNESCO's meeting in New Delhi.

beats.q: Which of these have you seen live?

In twenty twenty-one came Durga Puja in Kolkata, in West Bengal.
Then, in twenty twenty-three, Garba of Gujarat, a dance performed at Navaratri.
In twenty twenty-five, Deepavali joined, at UNESCO's meeting in New Delhi.
